findings.breaking_input: Run the new bats test on a fully green suite: part B prints `ok MUTANT FAILs driver-only: the harness claude as the command`, and assertion 52 REQUIRES that exact line, while assertion 50 requires `[[ "$output" != *"FAIL"* ]]` — "FAILs" contains "FAIL", so the test is unsatisfiable and can never pass.
findings.why: The phase's own RED-first gate is self-contradictory: one assertion demands the substring FAIL be absent and another demands a line containing FAILs be present. CI is permanently red on a good tree, or someone 'fixes' it by loosening the no-FAIL guard and the vacuous-pass protection dies.
findings.fix: Anchor the guard to the refusal prefix, e.g. `!= *'FAIL '*` (FAIL followed by space, which ok-lines never carry), or have the suite print mutants as `ok MUTANT rejected by driver-only: …` and assert that.
findings.twin_of: Tests that could not fail, or could not pass -> the mutant is the negative control; write the check it fails.

findings.breaking_input: Session review-ship.review starts; its run.log contains a line where arc-run echoes a foreign spine id (e.g. `waiting on 01M2TPXZ16FDQ07K3SWBJ6V44M`) or a receipt line naming kind `ship.done` for an id the spine holds as `note.logged` from another process. ULID_ANYWHERE/RECEIPT_LINE collect it, newness passes (minted after start), and attach serves it in this session's receipts — named:true, payload scrubbed and shown — though the spine event is another run's, of another kind, from another process.
findings.why: Attribution is by printed id + existence + newness only. The kind the receipt line NAMES (stored in `named`) is never compared with ev.kind, and ev.process is passed through without being checked against meta.process — exactly the checks the fixed-defect row demands. Any bare ULID the run prints (observed events, plan ids) is silently promoted to this session's receipt.
findings.fix: In receiptsOf, drop ids whose spine event's kind differs from the kind the line named (for RECEIPT_LINE hits), and require ev.process === meta.process before serving; bare-ULID hits are not receipts at all.
findings.twin_of: A receipt found by 'newest of the kind' is anybody's receipt -> attribute by the id the TOOL PRINTED, checked on the spine for kind, process and newness; no printed id, no receipt, never a guess.

findings.breaking_input: Plant a junction/symlink named AAAAAAAAAAAAAAAA inside journalDir/sessions pointing at another tree's session directory whose session.json has a numeric startedAt and a pid. GET /api/sessions lists it with the foreign session/process/driver/startedAt and its state (reading its exit.json and probing its pid with kill(pid,0)), while GET /api/session-run/AAAAAAAAAAAAAAAA refuses the same directory with RUN_OUTSIDE.
findings.why: The junction guard the file itself documents lives only in dirOf, which read() uses; list() walks sessionsDir and calls stateOf with no realpath containment or type check, so the door serves metadata and state from a tree it refuses to read.
findings.fix: Route list()'s per-run state through the same containment check as dirOf (or a shared containedDirOf), and skip/refuse uncontained entries by name.
findings.twin_of: Directory walks with no containment and no type check -> every file AND directory a route reads is realpath-contained and type-checked, exactly as `lanePhases` is.

findings.breaking_input: Once the engine lane adds processes/ship-run.process.yaml (the phase table's own plan), POST /api/session/review-ship.ship/start with one minted click spawns the whole ship-run process; nothing between the click and the deploy step reads confirmStep — grep the diff: the field is written on the row and surfaced by sessionsView, and no code in session-door.mjs start() or anywhere else ever reads it.
findings.why: The row promises 'its session stops for the owner's confirmation before the deploy step', but the confirmStep field is data no code enforces — the ADR-clause-without-a-check class. The spec's exit criterion ('a fixture proves no deploy step runs without it') has no door-side mechanism to fail.
findings.fix: Either enforce confirmStep in the door (start refuses past the confirm step without a second spend/token naming the step) or record the field as display-only with the enforcement named where it lives (the process file), and pin whichever with a fixture.
findings.twin_of: ADR rules no code enforced -> every clause of the ADR the wiring cites is a check or a refusal, by name.

findings.breaking_input: `mkdir processes/qa-run.process.yaml` (a directory, not a file). existsSync passes, GET /api/sessions reports qa processReady:true, and start spends its click and spawns arc-run with --process qa-run — which then fails on the unopenable 'file' with an unlabelled engine error instead of NO_PROCESS.
findings.why: processFileOf gates the NO_PROCESS refusal with existsSync, which accepts directories; sessionDrivers() and processNames() have the same hole (a directory named mock.mjs or x.process.yaml counts as a driver/process). The twin row was fixed elsewhere with isFile().
findings.fix: Use statSync(p).isFile() in processFileOf and filter processNames/sessionDrivers on isFile too.
findings.twin_of: `existsSync` accepted a directory as an executable, and a spawn error was an unhandled `'error'` event -> require `isFile()`, and every spawned child gets an `'error'` listener before anything else.

findings.breaking_input: Start any session and read the journal: the line is {"ts":…,"session":"council.convene","phase":"start",…}. The wrapper's `session: true` channel marker is overwritten by `...entry` (whose session key is the id) on every session-door journal line, so no line ever carries the marker the code writes it for — unlike the work door, whose `work: true` survives.
findings.why: Two sources for one key with the marker dead on arrival: any journal consumer keying the door channel the way `work: true` intends misclassifies every session start/end entry.
findings.fix: Name the marker distinctly (e.g. `sessionDoor: true`) or spread the entry first and add the marker after, so the two do not collide.

findings.breaking_input: POST /api/session/review-ship.review/start with body {click:T, input:{}, bogus:1} where T is a live token: the unknown-key loop throws BAD_SESSION_BODY before spend() runs, so the door answers 400 with T still unspent and spendable — the pinned invariant 'a bad body still SPENDS its click: one click can never be retried' holds only for the validateInput arm the fixture covers, not for this one.
findings.why: The spend-first rule stated in the comment (and pinned by part C) is ordered after the key-shape check, so the two bad-body paths disagree on the invariant; the fixture never pins the unknown-key path.
findings.fix: Move the key-shape check after spend(), or drop the 'always costs the token' claim and pin both paths explicitly.
findings.twin_of: A guard that skips on an odd input is a guard that opens on it

findings.breaking_input: driverOnly({script:"engine/arc-run.mjs", args:["--process","p","--driver","auto","--transcript-dir",""]}, DRIVERS) returns null (accepted); so does a trailing ["--transcript-dir","--driver"] — a flag-shaped value. The mutant list pins --driver empty/unknown but the FREE_VALUE flags accept empty and flag-like values.
findings.why: The ADR-1326 gate refuses empty values only where the regex happens to catch them; the fixed flag rules require an empty value and a value starting with `--` to be refused for every flag.
findings.fix: In the pair loop, refuse an empty value for every flag and refuse any value starting with `--` for FREE_VALUE flags.
findings.twin_of: A flag consumed the NEXT flag as its value -> a value that starts with `--` is refused.

findings.breaking_input: Start memory.promote-rule on a verbose driver: the run prints `arc-run: receipt approval.requested <id>` early, then writes 300 KiB more output. Attach reads only the last 256 KiB, so receiptsOf never sees the line and the response shows receipts: [] for a session whose approval receipt the spine holds, while bytesDropped (~44k) says lines were cut but nothing says the receipts figure covers only the tail.
findings.why: Receipts are derived from the trimmed read and presented as THE session's receipts; a measurement over a partial log is drawn as complete for the field the door exists to guarantee.
findings.fix: Keep receipt lines out of the trim (scan the whole log for RECEIPT_LINE, or persist printed receipt ids at start-time sidecar) and label the receipts figure with the window it was read from.
findings.twin_of: Output dropped by a cap with nothing saying so -> every body carries what its cap dropped, and the page draws it.

findings.breaking_input: A run appending to run.log while attach polls: statSync reports size S, readFileSync then returns S+G bytes, so bytesDropped = max(0, S−LOG_TAIL) understates the true dropped count by G and the served tail exceeds LOG_TAIL; if the cut offset lands mid-UTF-8 the tail's first character becomes U+FFFD.
findings.why: Two reads of a growing file are mixed: the cap figure is computed from one read and the content from another (validate one read, compare another), and the byte cut is character-blind.
findings.fix: Compute bytesDropped from buf.length (the read actually served) and align the cut forward to a UTF-8 boundary before decoding.
findings.twin_of: The read host checked one read of a getter and keyed another -> copy once, then judge and use the copy.

findings.breaking_input: Kill the door mid-write so sessions/DDDDDDDDDDDDDDDD/session.json is half-written (or craft startedAt as a string): the run vanishes from GET /api/sessions forever with no unreadable count, while attach by id still serves it — the list and the attach disagree silently.
findings.why: Malformed or torn session metadata is dropped by the filter with no named finding; unreadable-because-torn and absent are different results served as one.
findings.fix: Collect dropped dirs into an `unreadable` count on the list response, named by sid, like the door's other unreadable-row rules.
findings.twin_of: A malformed id dropped silently -> malformed input is a named finding, never an omission.

findings.breaking_input: The second writeFileSync(session.json) (with pid) throws — disk full, or the directory removed right after spawn: the caller gets an untyped 500 INTERNAL, the child is already running detached, session.json keeps pid:null, and the error/exit handlers were never attached, so exit.json is never written and stateOf reports the live run as `ended` forever.
findings.why: Anything throwing between the spawn effect and the bookkeeping loses the run's identity: the line after the effect can be lost and can turn a started session into an untracked one.
findings.fix: Attach the error/exit handlers and write pid in a path that cannot silently skip them (register handlers before the pid write; on throw, journal a start-with-unknown-pid entry rather than surfacing INTERNAL).
findings.twin_of: An id line that throws after the write -> the line after the effect can be lost; it can never turn the effect into a refusal.

findings.breaking_input: `node .claude/scripts/hq/face-sessions.mjs --help` on the Windows leg: process.exit(2) fires immediately after the stderr usage write, racing libuv teardown — the fixed-defect row for every new CLI in this repo.
findings.why: A new CLI was written with process.exit() after the repo fixed the same call in face-tokens, face-coverage and the emitters: exitCode, never exit().
findings.fix: Set process.exitCode = 2 and return, letting the loop drain.
findings.twin_of: `process.exit()` raced libuv teardown on Windows -> set `process.exitCode` and let the loop drain.

findings.breaking_input: Run `node tests/face/session-door.mjs | cat` on a loaded CI leg: console.log('RAN: … checks') to a pipe is asynchronous and process.exit(...) on the next line can truncate it — the bats wrapper's required RAN guard intermittently reads as 'the suite did not finish' on a green run.
findings.why: The one line every caller parses sits behind process.exit — the exact emitter twin already fixed elsewhere; the exit code races the same flush.
findings.fix: Set process.exitCode and let stdout drain, or write the RAN line via a flushed synchronous path before exiting.
findings.twin_of: The emitter's own id line behind process.exit -> the twin of the process.exit row, in the one line every caller parses.
